title: Split pea and parsnip stew with purple sprouting broccoli

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a cupboard basic, and vegetable stock is explicitly allowed.

supermarket.reason: Yellow split peas, parsnips, purple sprouting broccoli and lemons are all everyday items at Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded pan, a sieve and a grater, and the technique is simple simmering.

works.reason: 250g split peas in 1.2 litres of stock simmered for about 50 minutes gives a thick stew for four, and the broccoli steams through on top in the time given.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes hands-on covers chopping an onion, peeling 500g of parsnips, trimming broccoli and zesting a lemon, and the simmering times add up to about 75 minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient is used and matches its id, and the only unlisted item is an optional splash of water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming pulse and parsnip stew suits mid-January, and the broccoli is a substantial 300g part of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Split peas, parsnips and greens make a filling, wholesome family dinner.
